title: TTS Serverless — Qwen3-TTS 1.7B + GigaAM-v3 (Russian voiceover)
description: RunPod serverless worker for the video_gen tts stand: one Russian phrase becomes 1–2 takes with the pinned Qwen3-TTS 1.7B Base model using Base voice cloning from an uploaded reference (preset voices do not exist in Base and fail visibly), with word timestamps and WER from GigaAM-v3. The worker never chooses a model (the model is the image and the attached network volume), ships no weights (pinned manifest, sha256 verified by populate-volume.sh) and returns the takes plus execution-fact telemetry (engine, engine version, aligner version, model hash, voice mode, reference hash, GPU seconds, license).

input.name: Job timeout (seconds)
input.description: Maximum time a single phrase job (synthesis + alignment) may run. Must be less than or equal to the endpoint timeout.

input.name: Max phrase length (characters)
input.description: Input phrase cap; longer text fails with input_invalid.

input.name: S3 endpoint
input.description: Optional S3/MinIO endpoint. Configure S3_* to return large takes as a presigned audio_url instead of inline base64.

input.name: S3 access key
input.description: S3/MinIO access key (secret — endpoint env only).

input.name: S3 secret key
input.description: S3/MinIO secret key (secret — endpoint env only).

input.name: S3 bucket
input.description: Bucket for large take output (alias: OUTPUT_BUCKET).

input.name: Auto-download models
input.description: Download the pinned Qwen3-TTS and GigaAM files listed in models-manifest.txt to the attached volume at worker boot (sha256 verified). Disable to prepare the volume manually.

changelog:
## v0.3.3

- Image size/build fix: base changed back to `pytorch/pytorch:2.7.1-cuda12.8-cudnn9-runtime` (~4.2 GB compressed) instead of `runpod/pytorch:...` (~7.9 GB compressed). The RunPod base was needed in v0.3.1 only for a Hub pull experiment but roughly doubled the downloaded layers; the Hub builder then spent more than the 30-minute build window on the CUDA base pull. torchaudio fallback now matches the base torch 2.7.1. The v0.3.2 cryptography `--ignore-installed` fix is kept.
- Unchanged: contract, handler, reference pipeline, engine and tests.

## v0.3.2

- Hub build fix: the RunPod PyTorch base ships a Debian `cryptography` 41.0.7 package without a RECORD file, so `pip install runpod==2.2.1` failed with `error: uninstall-no-record-file` when upgrading to `cryptography>=50`. The Dockerfile now installs `cryptography` and `runpod` with `--ignore-installed` (new copies in `/usr/local`, system Debian package is left intact), which removes the uninstall attempt.
- Unchanged: contract `tts-serverless/v1` clone/reference/telemetry, base image, handler, engine and tests.

## v0.3.1

- Hub build fix: default base switched from `pytorch/pytorch` to the RunPod PyTorch runtime `runpod/pytorch:2.2.0-rc.229-cu1281-torch291-ubuntu2404` (CUDA 12.8, torch 2.9.1). RunPod Hub GitHub builds pull this base through the RunPod registry/cache, avoiding the generic Docker Hub image pull that failed the v0.3.0 build. torchaudio is only installed when the base lacks it; qwen-tts/transformers/soundfile/librosa pins are unchanged.
- Unchanged: contract `tts-serverless/v1` clone/reference/telemetry, handler, reference download/verification, engine and tests.

## v0.3.0

- Base voice cloning (contract `tts-serverless/v1`, additive): input `voice` is now a `oneOf` — `{mode:"preset",speaker_id}` (kept for compatibility) or `{mode:"clone",reference:{url,sha256,text,language}}`. The reference arrives as a presigned HTTP(S) URL; the worker downloads it via httpx (timeout, ≤25 MiB), verifies sha256 and duration 1–15 s, decodes WAV/FLAC/MP3/OGG with soundfile/librosa, resamples to 24 kHz mono and calls Qwen3-TTS Base `generate_voice_clone(text, language, ref_audio=(np, sr), ref_text)`. Preset on Base fails visibly with `voice_mode_unsupported` — no silent fallback.
- Output telemetry additive: `voice_mode` (required) and `reference_hash` (verified sha256 of the reference, raw hex; null for preset). New visible error codes `reference_missing`, `reference_invalid`, `reference_hash`, `reference_too_large`, `voice_mode_unsupported`, `engine_failed`.
- Image: default base is now the pinned CUDA/PyTorch runtime `pytorch/pytorch:2.7.1-cuda12.8-cudnn9-runtime` with pinned `qwen-tts==0.1.1`, `transformers==4.57.3`, `soundfile==0.13.1`, `librosa==0.11.0` (torch from the base is never reinstalled). The `python:3.12-slim` structural build path stays via `--build-arg BASE_IMAGE=python:3.12-slim` (model runtime auto-skipped, no torch in the base). Hub: container disk 40 GB, host CUDA 13.2/13.0 (image CUDA 12.8).
- Engine: lazy model load from the pinned manifest on the volume; explicit author speed (`librosa.effects.time_stretch`), resampling to `render.sample_rate`, WAV PCM s16le; `ru` is mapped to the model language name `russian`.
- Version `0.3.0`. GigaAM-v3 aligner wiring remains `TODO(live)`; cloning is not yet verified on a live GPU endpoint.

## v0.2.3

- Hub build test: test GPU `NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3` (CUDA 13.2) instead of RTX 4090, which had no instances at build time; the test pod disables volume auto-population (no volume attached). Listing GPU pools include `ADA_48_PRO` and `ADA_80_PRO` so the test GPU is inside the published pools.
- Unchanged: contract `tts-serverless/v1`, handler, tests, manifest, entrypoint and volume auto-population.

## v0.2.2

- Live entrypoint: auto-populates the pinned volume at boot (`VOLUME_AUTOPOPULATE=true` by default; sha256 verified) and then starts the handler. A populate failure does not kill the container: health stays available and jobs fail with a visible `model_file_missing`. Hub env exposes `VOLUME_AUTOPOPULATE`.
- Unchanged: contract `tts-serverless/v1`, handler, tests, manifest. Qwen3-TTS/GigaAM live engine wiring remains `TODO(live)`.

## v0.2.1

- Hub build fix: the build test requested `12.8/12.9/13.0` and `gpuTypeId=NVIDIA L4`, but the L4 pool has no stock and the real host inventory (`GET /v2/catalog/gpus`) only has `13.2`, `13.0`, `12.6`, `12.4` — the test pod failed with `All returned supply constraints`. The test now uses a stock-bearing NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 (CUDA 13.2) and only real CUDA versions; listing pools widened to `ADA_24,AMPERE_24,AMPERE_48`.
- Unchanged: contract `tts-serverless/v1`, handler, tests, manifest and the CPU-only test image (no CUDA in the image). Engine/aligner live wiring stays `TODO(live)`.

## v0.2.0

- RunPod Hub listing metadata (`.runpod/hub.json`) and the build test (`.runpod/tests.json`, `action=health`).
- Health action (contract §3): `action: health` returns `{status, volume_mounted, engine, aligner}`. It only checks that the network volume is mounted and that the pinned engine/aligner files are present on it — no synthesis, no alignment, no weight hashing. Statuses `ok`/`starting`/`degraded` (volume mounted and models present / volume mounted but files still being populated / no volume).
- Input schema allows `action: health` without the phrase fields (additive within `tts-serverless/v1`); health contract examples and tests added.
- Version `0.2.0` (package, Dockerfile, Hub metadata); README documents the health action and Hub publishing.
- Unchanged: the generation contract `tts-serverless/v1`, telemetry facts, the pinned manifest and the normalization data. Engine/aligner live wiring and the CUDA image base remain `TODO(live)`.

## v0.1.0

- Initial release: contract `tts-serverless/v1` (one Russian phrase → 1–2 takes), Qwen3-TTS 1.7B Base + GigaAM-v3 build scaffold, pinned volume manifest + `populate-volume.sh`, normalization data, 123 GPU-free tests.
